To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) host preferences are common but rarely involve presence/absence of species; (b) the most important factors for diversity of decomposer fungal communities are characteristics of the substratum and the habitat, rather than host specificity; (c) the effects of disturbance on decomposer fungi depend on the group considered, and may be long lasting; and (d) the effects of anthropogenic disturbance on decomposer fungal communities may be mediated by indirect effects on host trees.

1) host preferences of tropical leaf decomposer fungi are common but usually do not affect species diversity of the decomposer community; 2) host preferences of wood decomposer fungi are rare, but their diversity is affected by the diversity of host trees and habitat heterogeneity; 3) disturbance can have long-lasting effects on fungal diversity in tropical forests; and 4) the diversity of decomposer bacteria and fungi are often negatively correlated with each other.
host-specificity and habitat heterogeneity are more important than host diversity in determining the diversity of decomposer fungal communities.

host preferences are not uncommon among tropical fungi that decompose litter or woody substrata, but their effects on fungal diversity are not always predictable.
host-specificity and host-diversity are important but not always the most important factors influencing the diversity of tropical forest decomposer fungi.

fungal diversity in tropical forest ecosystems is related to a variety of factors, including species richness and composition of host plants, disturbance and habitat heterogeneity, and the diversity of other decomposers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tropical forest decomposer fungi are diverse and host-specific, but not as host-specific as some other groups of fungi.

the decomposer fungi in the tropical forests we studied were more sensitive than their substrata or prey to disturbance and that they responded to changes in host diversity and habitat complexity more than they did to the host-specificity of their hosts.
the diversity of fungal decomposers in tropical forests is related to host diversity, habitat heterogeneity, and disturbance, but the nature of the relationships is not the same for all groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
decomposer fungi are diverse and their diversity is related to a variety of environmental factors that are important for their ecology.
decomposer fungi are very responsive to environmental change, so we should expect their diversity and composition to be highly variable over time and space.

the factors that influence the diversity of tropical forest decomposer fungi are diverse, complex, and context-dependent, and that we should be wary of sweeping generalizations about the factors that influence their diversity.
